AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testSparq.spec: RDF 1.2 N-Triples section 5.3 Grammar, productions [2] statement ::= directive | triple, [3] directive ::= versionDirective, [4] versionDirective ::= 'VERSION' versionSpecifier, [5] versionSpecifier ::= STRING_LITERAL_QUOTE; section 6.1: the version announcement is only a hint (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-triples/#sec-grammar)
AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testSparq.note: core.parse('VERSION "1.2--basic"', {format: 'ntriples12'}) rejects with term.invalid-iri 'expected subject (IRIREF or BLANK_NODE_LABEL) at line 1, column 1'; VERSION "1.2" is rejected the same way, and so is a VERSION line followed by a triple. turtle12 accepts the same directive. Expected: an empty graph.

AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testSparq.spec: RDF 1.2 N-Triples section 5.3 Grammar, [5] versionSpecifier ::= STRING_LITERAL_QUOTE (double quotes only; there is no STRING_LITERAL_SINGLE_QUOTE in the N-Triples grammar) (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-triples/#sec-grammar)
AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testSparq.note: RDF4J accepts VERSION '1.2--basic' in N-Triples; the grammar allows only a double-quoted version specifier, so rejection is correct. Factoidal rejects, but for the reason in the ntriples12-version-directive defect (no VERSION support at all); when that is fixed this case must still reject.

AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testDirLa.spec: RDF 1.2 Concepts section 3.4 Literals: 'If and only if the datatype IRI is http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#langString or http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#dirLangString, there is a non-empty language tag' (https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-concepts/#section-Graph-Literal)
AbstractNTriplesParserUnitTest#testDirLa.note: "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString has no language tag and no base direction, so no RDF literal can be built from it. RDF4J (VERIFY_DATATYPE_VALUES=false, its default) silently rewrites it to "Hello"^^xsd:string (RDFParserHelper.createLiteral); Factoidal rejects with term.invalid-langtag.
